title: Sequencer DB frame row must carry the same capture metadata as the FITS file
cause: Two sources of truth for one exposure. The FITS header was built from the Rust FrameContext (live per-frame telemetry) and that struct was then discarded; the captured_images row was built from ProgressDetail::FrameAccepted/FrameRejected, which carried only node_id, hfr, eccentricity, star_count and a path. The FrameContext now rides on the frame event as FrameCaptureMetadata, so both surfaces are stamped from one struct.

findings.claim: captured_images already HAS every column the task asked for
findings.evidence: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/tables/captured_images.dart:48-91 (gain, offset, sensorTemp, coolerPower, mountRa/Dec/Altitude/Azimuth, pierSide, focuserPosition, focuserTemp, rotatorAngle)
findings.consequence: NO schema migration was needed and none was added. Columns have existed since v18 and were simply never written by the sequencer path.

findings.claim: The FITS mount pointing was read a THIRD time, inside the bridge, not from FrameContext
findings.evidence: bridge/src/sequencer_ops.rs read_mount_pointing(), called unconditionally from save_fits
findings.consequence: FrameContext pointing now wins in build_rich_header, and save_fits skips the mount read entirely when the context carries it.

findings.claim: build_rich_header also let ImageData override the context's gain/offset/ccd_temp/exposure — a fourth source
findings.evidence: The new Rust agreement test FAILED on first run: GAIN card said 100 (ImageData) while the row payload said 139 (FrameContext)
findings.consequence: Those overrides are now fallbacks (only applied when the context field is unset). Byte-identical output for the sequencer path, which reconciles ImageData into the context upstream.

findings.claim: PRE-EXISTING, unrelated: the committed frb_generated.rs was stale, so any full FRB regen broke the Rust build
findings.evidence: git show HEAD:native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/frb_generated.rs | grep -c SimExposureRequest -> 0, while the struct is in committed source. First regen emitted E0308/E0277 resolving skotiq_native::camera::FrameType to crate::device::FrameType.
findings.consequence: Fixed at cause with #[frb(ignore)] on SimExposureRequest, matching its own doc comment ('Dart has no use for this').

tests.name: database_row_and_fits_header_agree_for_the_same_frame
tests.asserts: writes a real FITS file from one FrameContext, reads it back off disk, and checks GAIN/OFFSET/CCD-TEMP/EXPTIME/XBINNING/YBINNING/IMAGETYP/FOCUSPOS/FOCTEMP/ROTATPOS/RA/DEC against the FrameCaptureMetadata the row is written from
tests.revert_drill: restored the ImageData gain override in build_rich_header -> FAILED (GAIN card Some(100) vs row Some(139)); restored -> passes

tests.name: frame_event_carries_the_fits_writers_own_capture_context
tests.asserts: emit_grade_progress emits FrameAccepted whose capture payload equals FrameCaptureMetadata::from(the FrameContext save_fits got)
tests.revert_drill: changed capture: capture.clone() to capture: Default::default() -> FAILED (all-None/zero vs the real struct); restored -> passes

tests.name: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/sequence_frame_capture_metadata_test.dart
tests.asserts: 3 tests: accepted frame persists every capture field; rejected frame persists the same; a frame event WITHOUT the payload leaves the columns NULL (no fabricated zeros)
tests.revert_drill: restored the pre-fix insertSequenceFrame call (attribution-only, no new columns) -> 2 of 3 FAILED with row.gain == null, the reported defect verbatim; restored -> all 3 pass

verification.analyzer: 0 errors in skotiq_core, skotiq_bridge, skotiq_app, apps/desktop
verification.fmt: rustfmt clean on every file touched; dart format clean. bridge/src/api/post_session.rs has 3 PRE-EXISTING rustfmt diffs, untouched by this work.

not_done: No new FITS cards were added. mount_azimuth, pier_side and cooler_power are DB-only columns fed from the same struct; the FITS header has no OBJCTAZ/PIERSIDE/COOLERPW card and adding them was out of scope.
Not validated on hardware: the mount/pier/cooler reads in build_frame_context_for_save were exercised against NullDeviceOps, not a real driver.
